finding: Stale GallerySurface key for the deleted AssistantsSettings page — tsc fails in BOTH workspaces, so npm run check and npm run build are red.
resolution: I had fixed this once, verified tsc clean, then ran the generators and committed WITHOUT re-verifying — and the edit was gone. Re-applied and re-verified after the last mutation this time.

finding: Same stale key, found independently by running tsc in both workspaces.

register_routes is unconditional, so /api/run-js/mcp stays mounted with js_tool.enabled=false. Gated only on js_tool::use, which the Users group holds ⇒ arbitrary QuickJS execution reachable by any ordinary user while the kill switch says off.
resolution: Guarded register_routes; module struct defaults enabled=false so it fails closed.

finding: Items 1 and 2 do not match the design's own definition of disable ('does not serve the route'). web_search/lit_search register_routes unconditionally; only voice gates it.
resolution: Split each router: settings/admin REST always mounts (disable-only rows keep their admin UI), the MCP JSON-RPC endpoint mounts only when enabled.

finding: Revoking citations::use breaks chat for every non-admin: the citations backend chat extension attaches its tools + a system nudge to EVERY tool-capable chat with no permission check, so the tools are advertised and then 403.
resolution: Dropped all five revoke migrations. Fixing it properly needs a server-side kill switch for a UI-only item, which the design puts out of scope; the design's recorded limitation stands. DEC-4 reversed.

finding: Surviving hub UI: the onboarding MCP step renders a full 'Install from Hub' list gated only on HubMcpServersCreate, which admins hold via '*'. No lever reaches it — it lives in the SURVIVING onboarding module.
resolution: Gated on the same hidden-module list. Promoted on severity + INV-1 violation despite single-angle.

finding: The Playwright harness was not updated for the four flipped defaults (the Rust harness was), so every e2e run boots with all four OFF and the literature / web-search / lit-search sync suites lose their subject.
resolution: Harness now writes all four enabled, mirroring harness_inner.rs, with the asymmetry documented.

finding: Four surviving specs drive hidden features (permissions/hub, sync/hub-settings-sync, settings/js-tool-settings, perf/live-audit-ui-conformance).
resolution: Three deleted; the perf surface list had its hub + voice routes removed.

finding: Collateral deletion of SURVIVOR coverage: that file covered TWO entities, and api_key cross-device sync is unaffected by the reduction. No remaining sync spec covers api_key.
resolution: Restored the api_key half verbatim as sync/api-key-sync.spec.ts.

finding: Hollow INV-2 test: 'a project opens and its knowledge section still renders' never opens a project and asserts nothing about knowledge kinds. Passes unchanged if register() dropped EVERY contribution — the precise INV-2 break.
resolution: Creates a project and asserts 'Knowledge files' VISIBLE. Verified falsifiable: it failed until the owner-scoping bug below was fixed.

finding: Same defect: asserts on /projects (the LIST page) where knowledge kinds never render, and the docblock's claimed positive control ('Knowledge files' present) does not exist in the test.

HIDDEN_LABELS keyed on strings that do not exist ('Knowledge Bases' vs the real 'Knowledge'), and four of six are admin-gated slots invisible to the spec's permission-less user on main too — vacuous either way.
resolution: Real labels, more entries, and the sweep now runs as an ADMIN.

finding: All-negative route test with no positive control, and satisfied even if the hidden page rendered in FULL — it only asserts the 403 testid is absent.
resolution: Added a surviving-route control plus a per-route assertion that the feature's own content is absent.

finding: The chunk tracker cannot see the six hub sub-modules: chunkFileNames emits module.hub_modules_installed.<hash>.js, which the 'hub' regex does not match.
resolution: Added HIDDEN_SUBMODULE_CHUNKS.

finding: VoiceModule::new() hardcodes enabled:true with a stale comment; any path registering routes without a successful init fails OPEN and mounts the whole voice surface.
resolution: Fails closed now; same for the three modules that gained the field.

finding: Last hand-rolled copy of the resolution expression the new Config accessors exist to replace; and the bio_mcp unit test re-implemented it inline, so it could only confirm its own arithmetic.
resolution: Added Config::bio_mcp_enabled() and moved both sites onto it.

finding: Race in the positive control: the built-in row upsert is a fire-and-forget tokio::spawn, so querying immediately after the server reports healthy can lose it. Flaky, not vacuous.
resolution: Polls for the table to populate.

finding: assert_eq!(x, false) trips clippy bool_assert_comparison; and the comment overstated what the decorative lazy pool proves.
INV-5 overstated: the header claims 'nothing else is required' to restore a feature, which is false for the migration-based item 3 and (at the time) the five revokes.
resolution: Header now states the server-config and DB-default caveats and the e2e-deletion consequence.

finding: Latent pre-existing bug exposed by this diff: the test sorts its expectation by order alone while create_modules sorts by (order, name), so the expectation was LINKER-dependent and failed once these edits perturbed link order.
resolution: Expectation now uses the implementation's key.

finding: Every new e2e spec ran only as a permission-less user, so admin-gated hidden surfaces were absent regardless of the change. This is why a surviving hub surface slipped through.
resolution: The label, route and onboarding sweeps now run as an ADMIN.

finding: Deleting ~142 e2e spec files for merely HIDDEN features conflicts with INV-5: restoring a predicate restores the feature with zero e2e coverage.
resolution: Owner's explicit decision, taken after I raised this exact tension and offered relocation as a same-cost alternative. Recorded against INV-5 in DESIGN_FIDELITY rather than reversed unilaterally.

finding: Cargo.lock gains a webkit2gtk edge with no manifest change in the diff — unexplained lock drift in a feature commit.
resolution: Pre-existing lock staleness on main picked up by a regeneration, not caused here; the main clone shows the same modified Cargo.lock before any of my edits.

finding: test_clone_on_signup_still_gives_a_new_user_an_assistant cannot go red for any change in this diff — nothing here touches the backend assistant module.
resolution: Kept deliberately: it guards DEC-2's boundary (remove the template SURFACE, not the mechanism). Its value is as a regression tripwire for the next person who reads 'remove assistant templates' more broadly, not as coverage of this diff.

finding: Positional parameter silently changed meaning: (assistant, isTemplate, isCloning) → (assistant, isCloning). Both surviving call sites pass false, so it is safe by luck.
resolution: Both call sites verified passing false; a stale caller would be a type-correct behaviour change. Noted in the drawer comment. Not worth a wrapper object for two call sites.

finding: web_search / lit_search admin settings pages remain visible but their runtime enabled toggle is now inert — a dead control.
resolution: Both are DISABLE-only rows in the design's item table; hiding their UI would exceed the design. Recorded as a stated limitation in the PR body instead.

finding: The openapi generators call init() with the real config, so config-gating register_routes makes the emitted spec config-dependent. With paws' defaults, `just openapi-regen` DELETES /api/voice/* and /api/js-tool/settings from both workspaces' openapi.json and types.ts. Invisible locally (types_ts_parity regenerates from the COMMITTED spec) — it only surfaces at the merge-gate's regen-parity check.
resolution: openapi-gen.yaml now forces every deploy switch ON. The spec must describe the API surface the codebase can serve, not one deployment's subset.

finding: bio_mcp has the identical unguarded-route shape the round fixed elsewhere — and the round TOUCHED this file without adding the guard. Boot enabled once (row upserted), then disable: init early-returns without clearing the row, the route stays mounted gated on bio::query (held by Users), the proxy reads the stale enabled row and spawns the sidecar ⇒ query terms egress with the switch off.
resolution: Guarded, fail-closed default. Not a paws item, but the same hole.

finding: The spec covering this round's headline UI fix is HOLLOW and would pass on main: loginAsAdmin completes onboarding, so /onboarding opens on step 0 (Welcome) and the MCP step never mounts. Its only control was app-root visibility, satisfied by any authenticated page.
resolution: Clicks through to the step and asserts onboarding-step-mcp-servers is VISIBLE as the control. Verified RED under mutation.

finding: Even reaching the step, the 'Install from Hub' heading is behind `hubServers.length > 0`, so an empty e2e hub catalog makes that assertion vacuous regardless of the gate.
resolution: Added a prose assertion (/from the Hub/i) that does not depend on catalog contents. The mutation probe confirmed it: the PROSE assertion fired, the heading assertion did not — exactly as predicted.

finding: The fix gated the section and list but left the intro sentence two lines above still reading 'or install new ones from the Hub' to any admin. Incomplete in the very file it touched.
Same guide points the admin at 'The Hub catalog' for embedding models.
resolution: Rewritten to the two routes that still work; model names kept as examples.

finding: The hub fetch is ungated inside a Promise.all while only the RENDER is gated. Beyond the wasted call: if the hub ever became unreachable for a user the rejection sets serversError and shows an error alert on the whole MCP onboarding step — breaking a surviving surface.

Stranded by this round: the harness now server-enables js_tool, but the js-tool chat extension is filtered out of the UI, and it is the sole registrant of the run_js_approval content type and SSE handler. Every testid the spec waits on comes from that component, so it cannot pass. Server-enabling a feature does not un-hide its UI.
resolution: Deleted, as settings/js-tool-settings.spec.ts already was. The sibling run-js specs assert generic mcp-toolcall-* ids and are unaffected.

finding: 10 of the 14 chunk assertions could not fail: the test ran as a []-permission user, and those modules' original predicates required Hub*/Voice/JsTool/FileRag perms, so their chunks would never be requested with or without the reduction. The sibling label test was switched to admin for exactly this reason; the file's own PRIMARY assertion was not.
resolution: Now runs as ADMIN and visits /hub so the location-scoped sub-modules would load if unhidden.

finding: /settings/scheduler silently dropped from HIDDEN_ROUTES during the tuple conversion, and HIDDEN_LABELS omits the admin-slot labels 'Scheduler' and 'System Workflows' — a partial restore would pass.
The poll breaks as soon as ANY built-in row exists, but the caller asserts three SPECIFIC rows; memory/files landing first satisfies the poll while the three targets are still in flight.
resolution: Closed: the poll now waits for the SPECIFIC names the caller asserts on, not merely for any row.

finding: Stale docstring still claiming 'the reduction only ever REVOKES grants' after the revokes were withdrawn — the last claim in the tree that revokes ship.
The grants pin covered 2 of ~12 withdrawn grants, so a future round could re-revoke the hub grants and stay green.
resolution: Pins all ten.

finding: Docstring premise false after the withdrawal: claims the user LACKS citations::use via a DEC-4 revoke that no longer ships.
'No feature code was deleted' reads as a blanket claim in the reduction's source of truth, but items 12/13 did delete code.

The admin 'Enable web search' toggle saves and persists but does nothing — the deploy switch overrides it and no UI copy says so. Same for literature. Mirrors the very confusion the design warns about (implying enabled == on).
resolution: Honest disclosure needs the UI to learn the deploy switch state — a new capability endpoint, i.e. new surface area on a DISABLE-only row the design deliberately leaves untouched. Recorded as a stated limitation in the PR body instead of quietly growing scope.

finding: control_mcp still hand-rolls the resolution expression and its new() defaults enabled:true — the pattern this round changed elsewhere with the reasoning that a stale initializer defaulting a kill switch ON is how a switch gets bypassed.
resolution: Harmless today (its config default IS true, and its register_routes already guards). control_mcp is not a paws item; changing it would widen the diff into an unrelated module for a latent-only issue. The overclaiming comment in config.rs was narrowed instead.

finding: Drawer title still reads 'Create from Template' on the clone path — the last user-visible 'Template' string.
resolution: Accurate for what that path does (cloning), and the path is unreachable anyway since nothing sets isCloning. Renaming it would be churn on dead code.

finding: init early-returns before upsert_builtin_server, so an mcp_servers row from a prior enabled boot survives with enabled=true and a URL that now 404s. The chat extension is config-gated so it will not attach.
resolution: Pre-existing shape shared by every built-in MCP module (none reconcile stale rows on disable). Reconciling it is a general change to the built-in registration contract, not this feature's business — and with the route now unmounted the row is inert.

finding: My round-2 bio_mcp route guard BREAKS five existing integration tests. The harness defaults bio_mcp_enabled:false, so every test server now has /api/bio/mcp unmounted and the tests asserting 401/403/503/405 get a bare 404. tests/bio_mcp/ was not touched by this branch.
resolution: REVERTED the guard. bio_mcp is not one of the 13 items — this was my scope creep. Unmounting changes its disabled contract, and one of those tests deliberately relies on the disabled path to reach the graceful-503 branch; redefining that contract belongs to whoever owns bio_mcp. Recorded as a follow-up in the PR body, with the reasoning left in the code as a comment so the next person does not re-add it blind. All 14 bio_mcp tests pass again.

finding: Substring-shadowed assertions: blob.contains("hub::assistants::read") is satisfied by hub::assistants::read_version, which the SAME migration grants. A future array_remove of the exact grant would leave this green.
resolution: Parses the permissions arrays and matches exactly, with a non-empty guard so the loop cannot pass vacuously.

finding: The onboarding prose assertion can pass during the step's loading branch: the onboarding-step-* wrapper is rendered OUTSIDE the step component, so the positive control goes green while the body is still a spinner and both absence assertions resolve trivially.
resolution: Waits for the surviving sentence to be visible before asserting absence.

finding: 'No skills installed yet — browse the Hub to install one'. The skill module SURVIVES and a fresh paws instance has no skills, so this is the DEFAULT state of /settings/skills — the most visible surviving pointer to a hidden feature.

A SURVIVING sidebar widget reads HubModels.$, and that store is a lazy proxy that initialises on FIRST ACCESS — so the read fires GET /api/hub/models, /api/hub/models/version and /api/hub/local-providers for a feature with no UI. Exactly the render-gated-but-fetch-ungated hazard I wrote a paragraph about in loadMcpServers and did not fix here.
resolution: Hub lookup short-circuits when hub is hidden, so the store is never touched; the fallback path was already correct. Error copy gated too.

finding: Runs unconditionally on every assistant message and rewrites any bare [n] into a role=button, tabIndex=0, aria-labelled citation chip whose handler looks for a kb-tool-result-card that cannot exist — a dead but focusable, screen-reader-announced affordance for a hidden feature, in chat CORE. Ordinary prose containing '[1]' produces one.

INV-5 violation I introduced in round 2: I rewrote the Hub sentence IN PLACE instead of gating it, so deleting 'hub' from the list would restore the hub everywhere except here — a code edit needing manual revert, which is what INV-5 forbids.
resolution: Now gated like its sibling one file over.

finding: The header still enumerated FOUR consumers after round 2 added two more — and this enumeration IS the audit-and-revert surface INV-4/INV-5 promise.
resolution: Rewritten to describe the classes of consumer and to point at the grep that gives the authoritative set, rather than a count that goes stale.

finding: Live admin copy on the surviving /settings/mcp-servers page describes 'the MCP tab in the Hub', including an Alert title.
Live form tooltip on a surviving page names two hidden features ('Document RAG / knowledge bases').
Page subtitle names 'scheduled loops you started' — the scheduler is hidden, so no UI can start one.

control_mcp defaults ON and builds its catalog from the LIVE router, which still mounts all of workflow/scheduler/citations/knowledge_base/file_rag/hub REST — and the grants were deliberately kept. So the model can list_capabilities and invoke_capability against hidden features. The design frames the residual as 'a user who knows the URL'; in practice the MODEL enumerates them.
resolution: ESCALATED, not absorbed. Closing it means either a server-side kill switch per UI-only item (explicitly out of scope) or revoking grants (withdrawn in round 1 because it breaks chat). This materially sharpens the design's stated limitation and belongs to the owner, so it goes in the PR body and HUMAN_FEEDBACK rather than being quietly fixed or quietly dropped.

finding: Admin help text names 'workflow agent steps' and 'the scheduler's horizon backstop'.
resolution: Accurate description of what those AGENT settings do — the agent module genuinely has a workflow step kind and a scheduler horizon, and those settings still function. Renaming them would misdescribe the setting to make a string disappear.

finding: Still calls ApiClient.Hub.createMcpServerFromHub ungated.
resolution: The loop iterates selectedMcpServerIds, which can only be populated from the now-ungated hidden section, so it is unreachable. A guard here would be noise on dead code.

finding: Two comments still cite the deleted run-js-inner-approval.spec.ts as covering pointer-events inerting; that channel is now genuinely uncovered and the comment says otherwise.
resolution: Closed: the comment now states the spec was DELETED and that the CSS-inerting channel is uncovered, instead of citing it as live coverage.

finding: memory's own semantic-search toggle survives fully visible; if design item 3 meant 'semantic search' generically it is half-delivered.
resolution: The design's mechanism column names file_rag_admin_settings.semantic_enabled explicitly, so item 3 is file-RAG semantic search. Memory recall is a different subsystem the design does not list. Following the design's own words rather than a broader reading of the row title.

finding: The round-3 citation gate makes citationTokenize a no-op, but citationTokenize.test.ts still asserts the tokenizing behaviour — a test I broke and did not update. Both angles reproduced it by running: 26 failures at HEAD vs 25 with the one line removed.
resolution: citationTokenize now takes the injectable hidden set its own helper advertises. The regex-rule cases inject an empty set so they keep testing tokenization; a new case asserts the paws behaviour against the REAL list, which is the assertion that goes red if the gate is removed. 3/3 pass.

finding: The new JSX ternary in MemorySetupStep adds a RequiredState signal, so check:state-matrix is RED at HEAD — the first genuinely new key (earlier staleness was line-number shifts only).
resolution: Regenerated; check:state-matrix and check:gallery-coverage both PASS.

finding: The gate key does not match the features named: the copy names Document RAG (item 10, file_rag) AND knowledge bases (item 9, knowledge-base) but gated on knowledge-base alone. Restoring one would re-advertise the other while still hidden — the asymmetry INV-5 exists to prevent.
resolution: Composed both keys.

finding: The header still said 'hidden in FOUR places' and 'delete its entry from the two sets' — stale in the very commit that added 'Keep this enumeration current', and stale again one round after I last fixed it.
resolution: Stopped enumerating files and counts entirely; the header now names the CLASSES of consumer and points at the authoritative grep. A count that went stale twice in consecutive rounds should not be maintained by hand a third time.

finding: Two admin descriptions name hidden features ('workflow agent steps', 'the scheduler's horizon backstop') while three sibling copies were gated — inconsistent by the round's own standard.
resolution: SPLIT rather than treated alike. Gated the workflow clause (it names a surface the user cannot reach — no workflow can be authored). Left the scheduler sentence: its horizon backstop is a server-side ceiling that still applies whether or not the scheduler has a UI, so trimming it would misdescribe the setting to make a string disappear.

finding: The tokenizer is gated but the RENDERER is not: literal '[1](#kb-cite-1)' in assistant text still renders the dead focusable chip via a narrower door.
resolution: Requires the model to emit the exact internal href form, which nothing instructs it to do; the tokenizer was the only path that manufactured them. Gating the renderer too would add a second gate for a path with no producer. Recorded.

finding: Doc sentence 'there is nothing to wait for' described the OLD expect_any semantics; the empty-slice path still polls for any row.
The revert comment asserts a hardcoded count ('five existing tests') — the kind of count CODING_GUIDELINES §17 says to derive rather than assert.
resolution: Reworded to name the tests by kind, not by count.

finding: The comment's premise ('nothing can have been installed from the hub') holds for a FRESH instance but not for a deployment that ran with the hub enabled and was later reduced — those rows lose the gated hub-retry modals.
resolution: Comment now states the trade explicitly instead of asserting a no-op.

finding: None of the nine new call sites uses the injectable hidden-set parameter, so the non-hidden branch of each is untestable by injection.
resolution: citationTokenize (the one consumer that is a pure function) now does inject, and its restored branch is covered. The rest are React components where injection would mean plumbing a prop through purely for tests; their non-hidden branches were instead verified byte-identical to main by the auditor, which is the property that matters for INV-5.

finding: Registered store actions on a surviving module still call ApiClient.Hub.* with no non-hub caller — dead, not live.
resolution: Unreachable: nothing renders a caller. Gating dead actions adds noise; deleting them is feature-code deletion the design puts out of scope.
